correctness.rationale: For t fixed marked pair events, their horizontal-index graph with v vertices and c components permits O(n^c) choices of horizontal base indices and O(n^c) choices of vertical base values. The probability of a consistent injective assignment is 1/(n)_v. Every overlap component on >=3 vertices has total contribution O(n^{2c-v})=O(1/n), while t disjoint two-vertex components give spatial mixed factorial moments equal to products of rectangle areas. Expected fixed-mark counts are exactly (n-h)(n-k)/(n(n-1)) and remain bounded. The mixed moments and tightness yield independent unit-intensity Poisson point measures; finite lattice union counting yields joint distance probabilities; conditioning on a nonempty independent Poisson shell gives the uniform nearest-pair mark and anchor. The standalone Python verifier completed 364 exact tests through n=8. Finite checks do not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed independent unit-intensity two-dimensional spatial Poisson fields for all fixed distinct signed displacement marks are stronger than the already known unmarked Manhattan close-pair Poisson count and the isolated increasing-succession law. A 2017 theorem covers the Manhattan marginal exactly and that marginal is explicitly excluded from the novelty argument. The 2013 source covers the single increasing adjacent-consecutive-value mark; 2015 ordinal-pattern approximations do not fix numerical differences; 2016 prolific permutations connect a different geometric invariant. No inspected source states independence across the entire finite mark spectrum and location, or the joint Manhattan/max-coordinate law. Indexed records with closest titles either concern one adjacent mark or extreme corner positions. This is a best-knowledge judgment, not proof of exhaustive literature uniqueness.

value.rationale: The full finite-mark field is a motivated complete local collision invariant for permutation diagrams. It provides joint and spatial information not implied by the published scalar Manhattan and unseparated-pair laws: any fixed anisotropic exclusion zone has an exact limiting avoidance probability, the joint Manhattan/max-coordinate law has a nontrivial intersection correction, and the first closest-pair mark and anchor have an explicit conditional distribution. This connects permutation pattern breadth to quantitative spatial rank-matching defects without selecting an arbitrary finite parameter slice. The novelty credit concerns the full structural law and its genuinely joint consequences, not known marginals.
